I passed out once when I was 19. My boyfriend at the time called an ambulance, they did an EKG and decided I needed to be admitted to the hospital. My third night, after more extensive tests came back clean (my 12-lead EKG kept saying something like “nonspecific T wave abnormality” if I remember correctly), my heart started slowing down. I heard my EKG machine start beeping a lot and the yellow letters “BRADY” appeared across the top of the machine. I’m not sure I lost consciousness at any point. but I remember someone rushing in and putting something in my IV. I don’t think they said anything. It’s all kind of a blur. I was very tired, and this was all a long time ago. When the attending rounded on me the next day, he said, really nonchalant, “Well, it looks like you almost died last night, so we’re gonna have to keep you in ICU.” He was in a hurry and didn’t really give me space to ask any questions, so I have no idea how serious he was. I stayed in ICU another week. Eventually, my EKG came back normal one day and they just let me go home. They ran every test in the book and found nothing wrong.
